oidc_jwt.description: Reusing the same valid JWT to obtain multiple Vault tokens is allowed by design because Vault JWT auth is a stateless verifier and the docs do not describe jti replay tracking.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT/OIDC auth method API docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report replay of the same JWT as a freshness vulnerability unless the tested protocol layer explicitly promises one-time use.

oidc_jwt.description: The JWT auth login endpoint validates signed JWTs statelessly and does not document one-time JWT consumption or jti tracking.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT/OIDC auth method API: JWT login endpoint only verifies the signed JWT and role constraints; no replay cache or jti tracking is documented.
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same valid JWT to obtain multiple Vault tokens is expected behavior for this platform and should not be reported as a replay vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Token lookup-self display_name includes auth mount metadata as a prefix before the upstream identity value.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault token lookup-self example shows display_name like ldap2-tesla
oidc_jwt.note: The prefix reflects the auth mount path/name and should not be treated as an identity mismatch if the suffix matches the sent identity claim.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC provider with empty allowed_client_ids allows no clients; only '*' makes it universally permissive.
oidc_jwt.note: Empty allowed_client_ids causing denial is expected behavior, not an authorization bug.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC provider client with no assignments allows no Vault entities to authenticate through the client; allow_all must be configured to permit everyone.
oidc_jwt.note: Authentication denial for unassigned entities is by design and should not be mistaken for broken OIDC flow handling.

oidc_jwt.description: The auth mount's default_role is used only when the login request omits the role parameter.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT/OIDC config and login docs: default_role is used if none is provided during login.
oidc_jwt.note: Changing default_role will not affect tests that explicitly send role in login_with_jwt.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's identity OIDC provider requires PKCE for public clients in the authorization code flow.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault OIDC provider client docs: public clients must use PKCE for the authorization code flow.
oidc_jwt.note: A failed code exchange without code_verifier for a public client is expected hardening behavior, not a flow-coherence bug.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Exactly one global JWT trust source must be configured in configure_jwt_validation: oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do not set more than one, and do not leave all unset, or JWT/OIDC validation setup is invalid.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless you intentionally test the by-design unbound case. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim at all, so issuer-mismatch and trust-anchor-substitution tests become meaningless.
If configure_jwt_validation uses jwks_pairs, bound_issuer cannot be configured. Do not attempt issuer-enforcement tests with jwks_pairs because the platform forbids that combination.

create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. A valid role cannot be created with no constraints at all; use at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims when needed for setup.

For JWT roles, bound_audiences is required whenever the JWT contains an aud claim (the typical case), and the token aud must match at least one configured audience. For I5 audience tests, include bound_audiences in the role; otherwise empty_audience or audience_mismatch results may reflect misconfiguration rather than enforcement behavior.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only; there is no companion type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally, not as patterns. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting it to a wildcard.

bound_audiences is exact list-membership matching only; there is no companion type parameter. Wildcards are not documented and should be treated as literal strings. For I4 multi-identity scenarios needing multiple aud values, either provide all exact values or omit the audience restriction; do not use '*'.

bound_claims matching is controlled by bound_claims_type. With bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are treated as literals and must match exactly. With bound_claims_type='glob', '*' is wildcard. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple different claim values to pass the same role, either omit the exact-match claim constraint or explicitly set bound_claims_type='glob'; do not assume '*' works under the default mode.

bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type to 'glob' rather than the default 'string' so numeric JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching instead of being rejected outright by literal string handling.

For additional I5 numeric-type testing on bound_claims, test whether Vault truncates or coerces numeric JWT claims unexpectedly: configure a numeric bound_claims value N, then send a JWT claim with float N+0.7. If it matches, that indicates unsafe coercion. Use bound_claims with bound_claims_type='glob' to ensure the platform accepts numeric claims for the test path.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING claim value. If the selected claim is absent or non-string, login will fail. For I4 principal-binding tests, choose a stable string claim such as sub or another string-valued claim; do not use array/object/numeric claims as user_claim.

groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. For I4 type-confusion tests, a JWT groups claim sent as a bare string is expected to fail rather than aliasing like a one-element list; do not treat string-vs-list rejection as an identity-collision bug.

user_claim_json_pointer only changes how the claim path is interpreted; it does not change matching semantics. If you use JSON pointer syntax in user_claim, you must explicitly set user_claim_json_pointer=true or the literal pointer string will be treated as the claim name.
clock_skew_leeway has sentinel behavior: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds of leeway, while value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict zero-skew enforcement.
expiration_leeway has sentinel behavior: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds of leeway, while value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 means immediate expiration enforcement.
not_before_leeway has sentinel behavior: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds of leeway, while value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict nbf enforcement.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT alongside the attack JWT. Because leeway defaults are nonzero unless explicitly disabled with -1, an attack token near the boundary may still authenticate by design. Use {{now_epoch}}, {{now_epoch_plus_N}}, and {{now_epoch_minus_N}} claims and set the relevant leeway fields explicitly when testing strict freshness.

token_num_uses limits every API call made with the resulting Vault session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and a protected read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-bound verification calls are present.

JWT replay of the same signed JWT is stateless and by design unless the surrounding protocol adds one-time semantics. Do not flag replay_same_token or missing jti tracking as an I2 vulnerability for Vault JWT login; RFC 7519 jti tracking is optional and Vault docs do not describe JWT replay caches.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, rotate the actual trust anchor used by configure_jwt_validation (jwks_url, jwt_validation_pubkeys, or oidc_discovery_url-backed keys) and then perform a NEW login. A successful baseline login before rotation does not imply old tokens should remain acceptable after trust changes.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, omit the role parameter in login_with_jwt so the mount's default_role is exercised. If role is explicitly supplied, changing default_role will not affect the login and the test is invalid.

For I3 config-change sequences, NEW logins evaluated under updated config are by design. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of equivalent new requests before and after the admin change, not expect an already-issued Vault token to retroactively lose permissions without reauthentication.

OIDC role setup requires allowed_redirect_uris and OIDC callback requests must use a redirect_uri that exactly matches one of the configured values. For redirect_uri mismatch tests, ensure the baseline uses an exact configured URI first; otherwise failures are just setup errors.

In Vault's OIDC provider client configuration, redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in authorization requests. This is exact matching, not globbing. Do not use wildcard redirect URIs in OIDC flow tests.

Vault OIDC provider clients default to allowing no entities unless assignments are configured; to allow all entities, the client must include the built-in allow_all assignment. If you test Vault as an OIDC provider and forget assignments, authorization failures are by design and not token-exchange or scope-binding bugs.

Vault OIDC provider provider.allowed_client_ids defaults to allowing no clients when empty; '*' explicitly allows all clients. Empty is not a wildcard sentinel. Do not interpret an empty allowed_client_ids list as permissive.

Vault OIDC provider supports only authorization_code grant at /v1/identity/oidc/provider/{name}/token. It is not an RFC 8693 token exchange endpoint. Do not run token_exchange or cross-org token exchange attack patterns against this endpoint.

Public OIDC provider clients must use PKCE for the authorization code flow, while confidential clients may use PKCE optionally. For pkce_skip and pkce_not_required_public_client checks, assert rejection via non-200 status for public clients without code_verifier; do not compare identities.

OIDC provider token endpoint requires redirect_uri to exactly match the value used when the authorization code was generated. For state/code swap tests, keep all other parameters identical except the swapped binding artifact, or failures may be caused by redirect mismatch instead of session binding.

External identity groups should be used with group aliases for external auth-derived membership. While the generic group API accepts member_entity_ids/member_group_ids, JWT/OIDC external group mapping for groups_claim should be modeled via create_identity_group(type=external) plus create_group_alias, not by manually stuffing members into the group.

KV v2 list operations use the /metadata/ path, while reads use /data/. For access-policy tests, grant list capability on /metadata/ if you need listing, and read capability on /data/ for verify_read_secret. A policy that only covers /data/ will not permit list operations by design.

Exactly one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, and jwt_validation_pubkeys must be set in configure_jwt_validation. jwks_pairs is an alternate JWKS source and cannot be combined with jwks_url/jwks_ca_pem; bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. Misconfiguring these trust-anchor inputs invalidates I1 tests because the verifier may not be using the intended key source.

Every JWT/OIDC role must have at least one bound value configured. The role API states at least one bound value must be set. For JWT roles, use at minimum bound_audiences when the token contains aud; otherwise role creation or intended validation semantics may fail and I1/I5 tests become meaningless.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless the test intentionally exercises the no-issuer-binding case. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim, so forged-issuer tests can appear to 'pass' trivially because issuer validation was never enabled.

bound_subject supports exact string matching only; there is no companion bound_subject_type parameter. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely if multiple distinct sub values must authenticate to the same role. Setting bound_subject to '*' matches only the literal string '*'.

bound_audiences is exact list-membership matching against JWT aud; there is no wildcard/glob mode. For I5 audience tests, use concrete audience values. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, do not try to widen bound_audiences with '*' because it will be treated as a literal audience value, not a wildcard.

bound_claims matching mode is controlled by bound_claims_type. If bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are treated as literals and must match exactly. If bound_claims_type='glob', '*' is wildcard. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple claim values to pass the same role, either omit the relevant bound_claims entry or set bound_claims_type='glob' with an intentional pattern; do NOT set '*' under the default string mode because only the literal '*' will match.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on bound_claims, set bound_claims_type to 'glob' rather than the default 'string'. The docs state bound_claims may contain string, integer, boolean, or list values, but default string mode treats values as literals/exact matches; using glob is required so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings rather than being rejected outright before coercion behavior can be observed.

clock_skew_leeway has sentinel semantics for JWT roles: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds, while value -1 disables the extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict zero skew, and never assume -1 disables the underlying time validation itself; it only disables the added leeway buffer.

expiration_leeway has sentinel semantics for JWT roles: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, while value -1 disables the extra expiration leeway. Never use 0 when you intend an immediately-expired token test; use -1 for strict exp checking plus explicit exp claims such as exp={{now_epoch_minus_1}}.

not_before_leeway has sentinel semantics for JWT roles: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, while value -1 disables the extra not-before leeway. Never use 0 when you intend a strict future-token/nbf rejection test; use -1 and set nbf well into the future, e.g. nbf={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login in the same scenario using a valid JWT (for example iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, nbf omitted or <= {{now_epoch}}) alongside the ATTACK login. Without a control, a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from broken trust-anchor or role setup.

token_num_uses limits every API call made with the issued Vault session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the fuzzer performs both self-lookup and a protected-read check, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-bound verification calls are present. Setting token_num_uses=1 will exhaust the token during verification and cause false 403s on the access test.

JWT replay of the same signed JWT is by design for Vault's stateless JWT auth verifier. Do not flag replay_same_token or missing jti tracking as an I2 vulnerability for oidc_jwt. RFC 7519 jti tracking is optional and Vault's JWT login docs do not describe one-time JWT consumption.

For I3 config-change tests, NEW logins are evaluated against the current role/config at the time of login. A valid coherence test must compare behavior before and after an admin change using separate login attempts, not expect an already-issued Vault token to retroactively change. Use modify_role_config or configure_jwt_validation, then perform a fresh login_with_jwt.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, omit the role parameter from login_with_jwt so the mount's default_role is actually exercised. If role is explicitly supplied, changing default_role in configure_jwt_validation will have no effect and the test will be invalid.

For OIDC auth-code flow tests against Vault's auth method, allowed_redirect_uris on the role must exactly include the redirect_uri used by the client, and the callback request must carry the same redirect_uri context established by auth_url. Redirect URI matching is exact; mismatches are expected rejections, not identity bugs.

Vault's OIDC callback flow is session-bound by state, nonce, and optional client_nonce. For state_swap/code_injection style I3 tests, preserve the original auth_url outputs per session and only swap the targeted parameter; otherwise failures may simply reflect Vault's documented callback binding rather than a vulnerability.

Public OIDC clients on Vault's identity OIDC provider must use PKCE for the authorization code flow, while confidential clients may use PKCE optionally. For pkce_skip and pkce_not_required_public_client checks against the provider endpoints, assert non-200/error outcomes for missing code_verifier on public clients; do not interpret this as an identity mismatch test.

Vault identity group aliases are the supported way to map external JWT groups_claim values into internal identity groups. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, create an external identity group and bind it with create_group_alias using the JWT auth mount accessor; do not rely on member_entity_ids on the group to simulate external group membership.

External identity groups should not be manually populated with member_entity_ids for JWT-derived group membership tests. JWT groups are materialized through group aliases on the auth mount. Using direct membership on an external-group scenario can produce false positives for I5 because access may come from manual membership rather than the JWT groups claim.

Group policy application across namespaces is controlled globally by /sys/config/group-policy-application. The default mode within_namespace_hierarchy restricts when group policies apply; mode any relaxes this. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests in Enterprise/multi-namespace setups, record the current mode and do not misinterpret namespace-scoped policy application differences as authorization-binding bugs.

KV v2 list operations use the /metadata/ path, but secret reads use /data/. For verify_read_secret the path MUST be /v1/{engine}/data/{path}; using /metadata/ or KV v1-style paths will produce 404/permission differences unrelated to authorization.

KV v2 engine config max_versions has sentinel semantics: value 0 means keep the platform default of 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after also has sentinel semantics: '0s' means no automatic deletion timer. Do not assume zero disables storage or immediately deletes versions when constructing freshness or resource-lifecycle tests.
configure_jwt_validation MUST set exactly one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Vault rejects configs that set none or more than one of these trust sources.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless jwks_pairs is used. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault does not compare the JWT iss claim at all, so issuer-mismatch tests become meaningless. Also note bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set.

For I3 trust-anchor rotation tests, update the same auth mount config via /v1/auth/{mount}/config and then perform a NEW login. Vault applies new config to subsequent logins by design; do not treat admin reconfiguration itself as a flow-coherence bug.
Every JWT/OIDC role MUST have at least one bound value configured. Vault requires at least one constraint on the role; setup that omits all bound values will fail before any security test runs.

For JWT roles that contain an aud claim (the typical case), bound_audiences is required and the JWT aud must match at least one configured audience. For I5 audience tests, include a control token whose aud matches the configured bound_audiences; otherwise rejection may be caused by missing baseline setup rather than the attack mutation.

user_claim is required and its resolved claim value must be a string. Vault uses this value as the identity entity alias name. Tests that send non-string values in the chosen user_claim will fail as invalid setup, not as an identity-binding vulnerability.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only. There is no companion bound_subject_type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally, not as patterns. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple sub values to pass the same role, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting it to '*'.

bound_audiences performs membership matching against JWT aud values; it is not documented as glob or regex capable and has no _type companion. Treat it as exact-match only. For multi-identity I4 scenarios, do not try to widen it with wildcard strings; use a shared exact audience value across test tokens or omit aud from the attack dimension.

bound_claims matching semantics are controlled by bound_claims_type. If bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are treated as literals and must match exactly. If bound_claims_type='glob', '*' is wildcard-capable. For I4 multi-identity tests, exact-match bound_claims entries that vary across identities MUST be omitted, not set to '*', unless bound_claims_type is explicitly set to glob.

groups_claim must resolve to a list of strings. If the JWT supplies a scalar string instead of a string array, Vault setup/login behavior reflects claim-type mismatch, not a group-binding escalation. For I4 type-confusion tests, compare scalar-vs-array behavior explicitly and do not assume both are valid inputs.
clock_skew_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 is strict validation.

expiration_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables this extra leeway. For expired-token tests, do not set 0 expecting immediate expiry enforcement; use -1 for strict exp checking.

not_before_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables this extra leeway. For future-token/nbf tests, do not set 0 expecting strict nbf enforcement; use -1 for strict checking.

For I3 default-role-change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role and then Vault uses the mount's default_role. To test default-role coherence, first verify baseline behavior without role, then change default_role in configure_jwt_validation, then repeat the same no-role login. Supplying an explicit role bypasses the default-role mechanism and invalidates the test.

For OIDC callback tests via exchange_code_for_token, the callback request must carry the exact state, nonce, code, and optional client_nonce values bound to the prior auth_url flow. Mixing values across sessions is the intended state/nonce binding test; accidental mismatch will simply fail the flow.

Vault OIDC roles require allowed_redirect_uris and the callback redirect_uri must exactly match one configured value. For redirect_uri mismatch tests, keep all other parameters valid and mutate only the redirect URI binding; otherwise the flow may fail for unrelated setup reasons.

Public OIDC clients in Vault must use PKCE for the authorization code flow, while confidential clients may use PKCE optionally. For PKCE tests, choose client_type deliberately; omitting code_verifier for a public client is expected rejection, not evidence of a vulnerability.

OIDC provider clients default to no assignments, meaning no Vault entities are allowed to authenticate through the client. To build a working OIDC provider-side control flow, configure assignments explicitly or use the built-in allow_all assignment; otherwise authorization failures are by design.
OIDC provider allowed_client_ids on providers and keys has wildcard semantics only for the literal value '*'; empty means no clients are allowed. Do not interpret empty as allow-all during setup.

KV v2 verify_read_secret and seed_protected_resource paths MUST include /data/. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and returns 404 on KV v2 mounts, causing false negatives in authorization tests.
KV v2 list operations use /metadata/ paths, not /data/. If a policy is intended to permit listing for setup or verification, grant list capability on /metadata/ as well as read/write on /data/.

External identity groups should be used with group aliases for JWT groups_claim mapping. Manually setting member_entity_ids on an external group is not the intended external-group binding model and can produce misleading authorization results.

Group policy application mode can be globally configured to within_namespace_hierarchy or any. In Enterprise environments, cross-namespace group-policy effects may be by design when mode=any. I5 tests involving identity groups must account for this global setting before flagging policy escalation.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive identifiers. Vault warns that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby share privileges. I4 collision tests should treat alias reuse/merge as a real risk surface, not as harmless duplication.
